source.title: Learning to Perturb Hidden Representations for Generalizable Deep Learning

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper. Some figure text is garbled, but the relevant Table 1 is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares dropout-trained classifiers with cross-entropy baselines and reports test error, bearing on whether dropout lowers held-out error in the tested settings.
record.gate_note: The paper also compares LPA with Dropout and Manifold Mixup, but those comparisons test LPA against the methods, not the broader claim versions. No random-label memorization, width sweep, convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison, optimizer or batch-size comparison, magnitude-aware sharpness measure, or memorized-example removal is reported.
record.test_reason: Dropout-versus-CE comparisons measure V6 directly, including an extension to long-tail CIFAR classification. These are the study's own results, and the study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that LPA improves over the compared methods across balanced classification, long-tail classification, and domain generalization, and complements logit perturbation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates a new class-level hidden-activation perturbation method and includes Dropout baselines; the dropout configuration and its training details are not stated.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that LPA performance depends on perturbation layer and hyperparameters; it does not report dropout sensitivity.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.8.1 argues that LPA promotes flat minima through structured parameter perturbations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-perturbation training promotes flatness in a structured parameter neighborhood; this does not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness correlation or ranking.

record.problems: Dropout results are reported only for the balanced CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 settings in the supplied table. Dropout configuration is not stated, and no uncertainty estimates are given.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Fully connected classifiers, very small training sets, excessive dropout, and removing dropout and weight decay together with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

missing.what: ResNet-32, CIFAR-10-LT, imbalance ratio 100: dropout overall accuracy is 40.8% versus CE 39.5%; tail-class accuracy is 13.2% versus CE 12.6%. Add separate V6 rows for the two measures.
ResNet-32, CIFAR-100-LT, imbalance ratio 100: dropout overall accuracy is 25.2% versus CE 24.3%; tail-class accuracy is 8.2% versus CE 6.1%. Add separate V6 rows for the two measures.

record.verdict_notes: The record incorrectly says dropout results appear only in Table 1; Figure 2 also reports them. Section 4.1 supplies shared training details: SGD with momentum 0.9, weight decay 0.0005, and batch size 128; balanced classification uses 200 epochs with learning-rate decays. Dropout probability and placement are unspecified. Small improvements count as observed here because V6 claims a reduction in error without prescribing its magnitude; statistical significance is unavailable.
